title: Cartier equality
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension ($K=k(b_1,\dots,b_m)$ for finitely many $b_i\in K$). Then the $K$-vector spaces $\Omega_{K/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $H_1(L_{K/k})$ (first homology of the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $k[K]\to K$, [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]) are finite dimensional and $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k(K)=\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}-\dim_KH_1(L_{K/k}),$$ $\operatorname{trdeg}$ the transcendence degree (the cardinality of a transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]). In particular, if $K/k$ is finite then $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=\dim_KH_1(L_{K/k})<\infty$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07E1 (lemma-cartier-equality, line 8573) and its proof (lines 8580-8597, via Algebra Lemmas 07BV, 00S1, 00S7 and the dimension formula for a global complete intersection); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (07E1,more-algebra-lemma-cartier-equality)

proof.text: *A model of $K$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] $K/k$ has a finite transcendence basis $x_1,\dots,x_d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-complete-intersection-model] (Stacks 07BV and its proof, as the source's proof says) there are $n\ge c\ge0$ with $n-c=d$, a regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_c$ in $P=k[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ and an injective $k$-algebra map $\iota:A=P/I\to K$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, such that $A$ is a domain and $\iota$ induces a $k$-algebra isomorphism $S^{-1}A\cong K$, $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. We identify $K=S^{-1}A$ by it from now on. (The source computes $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=\dim A=n-c$ via Algebra 00P0 and the dimension condition of a global complete intersection; the equality $n-c=d$ with $d$ the size of a transcendence basis is given directly by the construction of 07BV, $n=d+1+r$, $c=r+1$, so the dimension of $A$ is not needed: see step 7.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8580-8584 (via Algebra Lemma 07BV, algebra.tex lines 44534-44559)

proof.text: *The naive cotangent complex of the presentation $\alpha:P\to A$.* Let $\alpha:P\to A$ be the quotient map, a presentation of $A$ over $k$ with kernel $I$, and $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha):I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_\alpha}A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}$, $g\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dg$, its naive cotangent complex [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Since $f_1,\dots,f_c$ is a regular sequence in $P$, $I/I^2$ is a free $A$-module with basis $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] (with $R=P$, $J=I$). $\Omega_{P/k}$ is free on $\mathrm dX_1,\dots,\mathrm dX_n$ with $\mathrm dg=\sum_i(\partial g/\partial X_i)\mathrm dX_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], so $A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}$ is free over $A$ on $1\otimes\mathrm dX_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] and $\mathrm d_\alpha(\bar f_j)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial X_i)\,(1\otimes\mathrm dX_i)$. Hence $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ is isomorphic to the complex $\delta:A^{\oplus c}\to A^{\oplus n}$ given by the matrix $\bigl(\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial X_i)\bigr)_{i,j}$; in particular $H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha))=\ker\mathrm d_\alpha\cong\ker\delta$ and $\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\alpha\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8584-8590 (the displayed complex; I/I^2 free on the f_j by Algebra Lemma 00LN since the f_j form a regular sequence)

proof.text: *$H_0$: the cokernel is $\Omega_{A/k}$.* Applying [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $k\to P$ and the ideal $\mathfrak a=I$ (so $C=P/I=A$) gives the exact sequence $I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_\alpha}A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{A/k}\to0$, $1\otimes\mathrm dg\mapsto\mathrm d\alpha(g)$. So $\Omega_{A/k}\cong\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\alpha\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta$ as $A$-modules (step 2).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1 (H_0 of NL is Omega, Algebra Section 00S0)

proof.text: *$H_1$: independence of the presentation.* Let $\gamma:k[A]\to A$, $[a]\mapsto a$, be the canonical presentation, with kernel $I_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $A\otimes_{k[A]}\Omega_{k[A]/k}$ is free on the $1\otimes\mathrm d[a]$ and $1\otimes\mathrm dg\mapsto\sum_a\gamma(\partial g/\partial[a])\mathrm d[a]$ identifies $\mathrm{NL}(\gamma)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] with $\mathrm{NL}_{A/k}$ of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], so $H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\gamma))=H_1(L_{A/k})$. Let $\varphi:P\to k[A]$ be the $k$-algebra map with $X_i\mapsto[\alpha(X_i)]$ and $\psi:k[A]\to P$ the one with $[a]\mapsto p_a$ for chosen $p_a\in P$ with $\alpha(p_a)=a$ (universal property of polynomial rings). Then $\gamma\circ\varphi=\alpha$ and $\alpha\circ\psi=\gamma$ (check on the variables), so $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are morphisms of presentations over the identity square of $k\to A$, and so are $\psi\circ\varphi$, $\mathrm{id}_P$ (from $\alpha$ to $\alpha$) and $\varphi\circ\psi$, $\mathrm{id}_{k[A]}$ (from $\gamma$ to $\gamma$). By clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality], $\psi_*\varphi_*=(\psi\varphi)_*=(\mathrm{id}_P)_*=\mathrm{id}$ and likewise $\varphi_*\psi_*=\mathrm{id}$. So $\varphi_*:H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha))\to H_1(L_{A/k})$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules, and $H_1(L_{A/k})\cong\ker\delta$ (step 2).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy, line 35274), (1), (2) and the final assertion (comparison with the canonical presentation), cited in the proof of More on Algebra 07E1 line 8590

proof.text: *Localization to $K$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-localization] (with $R=k$, $T=S$, $B=S^{-1}A=K$) $H_1(L_{K/k})\cong S^{-1}H_1(L_{A/k})$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] $\Omega_{K/k}\cong S^{-1}\Omega_{A/k}$, both as $K$-modules. Localization at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]: applied to the exact sequences $0\to\ker\delta\to A^{\oplus c}\xrightarrow{\delta}A^{\oplus n}$ and $A^{\oplus c}\xrightarrow{\delta}A^{\oplus n}\to\operatorname{coker}\delta\to0$ it gives $S^{-1}(\ker\delta)=\ker(S^{-1}\delta)$ and $S^{-1}(\operatorname{coker}\delta)=\operatorname{coker}(S^{-1}\delta)$. Since $S^{-1}(A^{\oplus m})=K^{\oplus m}$ and $S^{-1}\delta=\delta_K:K^{\oplus c}\to K^{\oplus n}$ is the $K$-linear map with matrix $\bigl(\iota\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial X_i)\bigr)$, steps 3 and 4 give $K$-linear isomorphisms $H_1(L_{K/k})\cong\ker\delta_K$ and $\Omega_{K/k}\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta_K$. (This is the source's statement that $\mathrm{NL}_{K/k}$ is homotopy equivalent to $\bigoplus_{j=1}^cK\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nK\,\mathrm dx_i$, on homology, which is all that is used.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8584-8592 (via Algebra Lemma 00S7, lemma-localize-NL, line 35692)

proof.text: *Counting dimensions.* $\ker\delta_K\subseteq K^{\oplus c}$ and $\operatorname{coker}\delta_K=K^{\oplus n}/\operatorname{Im}\delta_K$ are finite dimensional, so by step 5 $\Omega_{K/k}$ and $H_1(L_{K/k})$ are finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces. By rank–nullity [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] for $\delta_K$, $\dim_K\ker\delta_K=c-\dim_K\operatorname{Im}\delta_K$, and for the projection $K^{\oplus n}\to\operatorname{coker}\delta_K$ (surjective, kernel $\operatorname{Im}\delta_K$), $\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\delta_K=n-\dim_K\operatorname{Im}\delta_K$ (dimensions as in [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]). Subtracting, $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}-\dim_KH_1(L_{K/k})=n-c=d$ (step 1).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8592-8597 ('which is n - c and we win')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $d$ is the number of elements of a transcendence basis of $K/k$, so $d=\operatorname{trdeg}_k(K)$, the transcendence degree being the cardinality of any transcendence basis [def-kun-transcendence-degree]; with step 6 this is the Cartier equality. If $K/k$ is finite, every $b\in K$ is algebraic over $k$ ($1,b,\dots,b^{N}$ are linearly dependent over $k$ for $N=[K:k]$), so the empty family is a transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] (it is algebraically independent, and $K$ is algebraic over $k(\emptyset)=k$), $\operatorname{trdeg}_kK=0$ and $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=\dim_KH_1(L_{K/k})<\infty$.

split_report.summary: Proof written from More on Algebra 07E1 and the lemmas it cites (Algebra 07BV with its proof, 00S1, 00S7; tags checked in tags/tags). Seven steps: model A = k[X]/(f) with f regular and Frac A = K from the proof of 07BV (new unsplit node, created for this item); NL of the presentation is A^c -> A^n by the Jacobian (conormal of a regular sequence free, Omega of a polynomial ring free); coker = Omega_{A/k} (00RU leaf); H_1 independent of the presentation (00S1 via the existing presentation-functoriality leaf); localization to K: H_1 (new Mathlib leaf Algebra.H1Cotangent.isLocalizedModule, Stacks 00S7) and Omega (leaf), exactness of localization (leaf); rank-nullity; trdeg = d by the definition of transcendence degree. Departure from the source below the unit level: the source gets trdeg = dim A = n - c through Algebra 00P0 and the dimension condition of a global complete intersection; the construction of 07BV gives n - c = d directly (n = d+1+r, c = r+1), so dimension theory is not used. Added def-kun-transcendence-degree to stmt_deps (the statement's trdeg needs its independence of the basis). Statement unchanged. Both citers use only what the statement says (finite dimension of Omega for lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo-choose; equality of dimensions for finite K'/K for lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective).

lean.statement: theorem cartier_equality (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.FiniteType k K] : Module.Finite K (KaehlerDifferential k K) ∧ Module.Finite K (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K) ∧ Algebra.trdeg k K + Module.finrank K (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K) = Module.finrank K (KaehlerDifferential k K) ∧ (FiniteDimensional k K → Module.finrank K (KaehlerDifferential k K) = Module.finrank K (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K))
